newsitem.title: USA: Woolworth's June, July sales softer than expected.
newsitem.headline: Woolworth's June, July sales softer than expected.

text.p: Woolworth Corp said Thursday that sales for June and July proved to be softer than expected, particularly for the athletic group of stores.

"Not only were we competing against the Olympics of last year, we also encountered an increased promotional selling environment which made comparisons very difficult during the quarter," said Roger Farah, chairman and chief executive officer.

Woolworth, which announced in mid-July it would close its 400 "five-and-dime" stores across the nation, said that sales for the second quarter declined 6.7 percent, to $1.5 billion from $1.607 billion in the same year-earlier period.
It said the sales reflected in part 423 fewer stores from continuing operations on a year-over-year basis. Comparable sales declined 2.5 percent for the quarter, it said.
Sales for the six-months, meanwhile, declined 4.3 percent to $3.039 billion from $3.177 billion a year earlier, it said. Comparable-store sales for the six-month period declined 1.4 percent.

Excluding the effect of foreign currency fluctuations and sales from disposed operations, sales remained flat for the quarter and increased 2.5 percent for the six-months as compared to the prior year, it said.

The company said that its restructuring in connection with the closing of its general merchandise operations and conversion of about 100 locations to its Foot Locker and Champs athletic formats was proceeding according to plan.

It said that during the second quarter, it opened 48 stores, closed 66 stores and remodeled or relocated 75 stores. It ended the quarter with 7,117 stores in North America, Europe and Australia. This compares to 7,540 stores, excluding the U.S. general merchandise stores, at the end of the 1996 second quarter, it said.
